```{r Original Model}
source("part_two/preliminary_results.R", echo = FALSE)
```

We first seeked to fix model assumptions. Log (ln(x+1)) transform was conducted on right skewed data, and log transform was conducted on the LBFDGHPW (hours worked per week), shifted by 

```{r}
# handing skewness of the numerical predictors
transformed_model <- model_data |> select(LSM_01, all_of(relevant_predictors))

# fitting new model with transformed preds.
# PAADVVOL, PAA_15A is right skewed
# LBFDGHPW is left skewed
c_val <- max(transformed_model$LBFDGHPW) + 1 # for log(c-x) transformation to handel left skew
transformed_model$PAADVVOL <- log1p(model_data$PAADVVOL)
transformed_model$PAA_15A <- log1p(model_data$PAA_15A)
transformed_model$LBFDGHPW <- log(c_val - (model_data$LBFDGHPW))

skew_corrected_model <- lm(
  formula = LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL * GEN_05 + PAA_15A + LBFDGHPW + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + INCDGHH + EDDVH3 + FSCDVHF2 + DHH_SEX,
  data = transformed_model
)

generate_plots(skew_corrected_model, relevant_predictors, output_dir = "part_two/figures/transformed_model", pairwise_predictors = intersect(relevant_predictors, numeric_classes), model_data = transformed_model)

generate_plots(model, relevant_predictors, output_dir = "part_two/figures/original_model", pairwise_predictors = intersect(relevant_predictors, numeric_classes), model_data = model_data)

```

This seemed to correct the skews of the predictors well. However, the evidence of model assumption violations were still present. Next, the response (Life Satisfaction) was transformed using BoxCox transformation. A lambda value of around 2 was found, and thus a square transform was conducted. Normality was largely corrected and linearity left intact, but heteroskedasticity was still present. 

```{r}
# transformed_model <- transformed_model[which(transformed_model$PAADVVOL <= 25000), ]
# transformed_model <- transformed_model[which(transformed_model$PAA_15A <= 80), ]

# fitting boxcox on Y + 1 (avoids negative values)
library(car)
p <- powerTransform(model_data$LSM_01 + 1)

transformed_model$LSM_01 <- (model_data$LSM_01 + 1)^2

boxcox_model <- lm(
  formula = LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL * GEN_05 + PAA_15A + LBFDGHPW + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + INCDGHH + EDDVH3 + FSCDVHF2 + DHH_SEX,
  data = transformed_model
)

generate_plots(boxcox_model, relevant_predictors, output_dir = "part_two/figures/transformed_model", pairwise_predictors = intersect(relevant_predictors, numeric_classes), model_data = transformed_model)
```
From pairwise predictor plots, it can be seen that there is a fanning pattern between PAADVVOL and PAA_15A. Drop PAA_15A (since it does not really capture a person being active) and see how the plots look like.
```{r trying to remove PAA_15A}
# have to redefine relevent predictors to make plots
relevant_predictors_no_PAA_15A <- c(
  "PAADVVOL",
  "LBFDGHPW",
  "GEN_05",
  "GEN_01",
  "GEN_10",
  "INCDGHH",
  "EDDVH3",
  "FSCDVHF2",
  "DHH_SEX"
)
model_no_PAA_15A <- lm(
  formula = LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL * GEN_05 + LBFDGHPW + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + INCDGHH + EDDVH3 + FSCDVHF2 + DHH_SEX,
  data = model_data
)
generate_plots(model_no_PAA_15A, relevant_predictors_no_PAA_15A, output_dir = "part_two/figures/original_model_no_PAA_15A", pairwise_predictors = intersect(relevant_predictors_no_PAA_15A, numeric_classes), model_data = model_data)
```
Without transformations, the residual plots look to same. Now I will try to fix boxcox on the predictors instead (goal here is I don't want to transform response because I feel like the interpreting that would be hard)
```{r boxcox on preds without PAA_15A}
cont_preds <- c("PAADVVOL", "LBFDGHPW")

model_data_boxcox_preds <- model_data
model_data_boxcox_preds$PAADVVOL <- model_data_boxcox_preds$PAADVVOL+1

p <- powerTransform(model_data_boxcox_preds[, c("PAADVVOL", "LBFDGHPW")])
summary(p)

model_data_boxcox_preds$PAADVVOL <- (model_data_boxcox_preds$PAADVVOL_s)^(1/3)
model_data_boxcox_preds$LBFDGHPW <- (model_data_boxcox_preds$LBFDGHPW_s)^(2.25)

boxcox_model_no_PAA_15A <- lm(
  formula = LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL * GEN_05 + LBFDGHPW + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + INCDGHH + EDDVH3 + FSCDVHF2 + DHH_SEX,
  data = model_data_boxcox_preds
)

generate_plots(boxcox_model_no_PAA_15A, relevant_predictors_no_PAA_15A, output_dir = "part_two/figures/transformed_model_no_PAA_15A", pairwise_predictors = intersect(relevant_predictors_no_PAA_15A, numeric_classes), model_data = model_data_boxcox_preds)
```
After checking the plots, this didn't do anything. So we decided to keep the old method of fixing assumptions.


Next, we wanted to remove predictors to improve our model fit. We first compared two baseline models: 
- Reduced Model: Predicts self-reported life satisfaction (`LSM_01`) using main effects only.
- Full Model: Adds an interaction term between physical activity volume (`PAADVVOL`) and perceived mental health (`GEN_05`) to test whether the effect of physical activity depends on mental health status.

```{r initial-models}
# Fit Reduced Model 
model_reduced <- lm(
  LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL + GEN_05 + PAA_15A + LBFDGHPW + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + 
    INCDGHH + EDDVH3 + FSCDVHF2 + DHH_SEX,
  data = transformed_model
)

# Fit Full Model 
model_full <- lm(
  LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL * GEN_05 + PAA_15A + LBFDGHPW + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + 
    INCDGHH + EDDVH3 + FSCDVHF2 + DHH_SEX,
  data = transformed_model
)

# Partial F Test comparing the interaction term
anova(model_reduced, model_full)
```

The partial F test produces a high p-value (close to 1), indicating that the interaction term does not significantly improve model fit. 

Next, backward selection was conducted to remove non-significant predictors sequentially. 

```{r initial-diagnostics}
vif(model_full, type = "predictor")

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model_full, main = "Full Model Diagnostics")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
 Multicollinearity: Adjusted GVIF values are all below 2, indicating no multicollinearity issues.

Dropping (`PAADVVOL:GEN_05`)

model_no_interaction <- lm(

    INCDGHH + EDDVH3 + FSCDVHF2 + DHH_SEX,
  data = transformed_model
)

drop1(model_no_interaction, test = "F")

To further justify our choice of which predictors we decided to drop, we will do an All Possible Subsets of Model Selection method 
```{r all possible subsets model selection}
# install.packages("leaps")
library("leaps")
best <- regsubsets(LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL * GEN_05 + PAA_15A + LBFDGHPW + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + 
    INCDGHH + EDDVH3 + FSCDVHF2 + DHH_SEX, data = transformed_model, nbest = 2, nvmax = 11, really.big = TRUE, method = "exhaustive")
# nvmax default is 8, really.big is needed above 9 preds
summary(best)

#plotting for visualization
# note: with subsets(best, statistic = "adjr2",legend = FALSE) everything was overlapping and impossible to read

```{r all-possible-subsets-plot, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
# create the output folder if it doesn't exist
out_dir <- "part_two/figures/all_possible_subsets_selection"
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# helper: regsubsets plot with smaller, 30-degree-tilted variable labels
plot_rs <- function(fit, scale, main, label_cex = 0.7, angle = 30) {
  labs <- c("(Intercept)", fit$xnames[-1])
  plot(fit, scale = scale, main = main, labels = rep("", length(labs)))
  usr <- par("usr")
  text(x = seq_along(labs),
       y = usr[3] - 0.02 * (usr[4] - usr[3]),
       labels = labs, srt = angle, adj = 1, xpd = TRUE, cex = label_cex)
}

# draw the two panels (wrapped in a function so we can reuse it)
plot_subsets <- function() {
  op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(12, 4, 3, 1), cex.axis = 0.7)
  on.exit(par(op))
  plot_rs(best, "adjr2", "Adjusted R²")
  plot_rs(best, "bic",   "BIC")
}

# save to file
png(file.path(out_dir, "all_possible_subsets_selection.png"),
    width = 14, height = 8, units = "in", res = 300)
plot_subsets()
invisible(dev.off())

# also show it in the knitted document
plot_subsets()
```

Resulting subsetted model. From backward selection, we have kept predictors with have a significant linear relationship with LSM_01. From the plot after conducting all possible subsets selection, if we look at the BIC, it can be seen that the model with the highest ranking BIC that includes the interaction term PAADVVOL:GEN_05 (we care about this term since it is our research question). Is the model with the same predictors as what we got from backward selection. Therefore these were the models we decided to keep.
```{r final-model}
library(lmtest)
new_relevant_predictors <- c("PAADVVOL", "GEN_05", "GEN_01", "GEN_10", "PAADVVOL:GEN_05")

subsetted_model <- lm(
  formula = reformulate(new_relevant_predictors, response = "LSM_01"),
  data = transformed_model
)

# 1. Multicollinearity (VIF)
vif(subsetted_model)

# 2. Residual Diagnostic Plots
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(subsetted_model, main = "Final Model Diagnostics")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# 3. Coefficient Summary
coeftest(subsetted_model, vcov = hccm(subsetted_model, type = "hc3"))
```

To think about which predictors to add, we will first identify problematic points. The pattern of these points may highlight a missing predictor in our model. 

```{r identifying-problematic-points}
p <- length(coef(subsetted_model)) - 1 # Number of predictors
n <- nobs(subsetted_model) # Number of observations

# Outliers
ri <- rstandard(subsetted_model)

outliers_indices <- which(abs(ri) > 4)

# Leverage points
hii <- hatvalues(subsetted_model)

leverage_point_indices <- which(hii > 2*(p+1)/n)

# Influential Points: Cooks distance 
cooks_distances <- cooks.distance(subsetted_model)

cooks_problematic_point_indices <- which(cooks_distances > qf(0.5, p + 1, n - p - 1))

# Influential Points: DFFITS
dffits <- dffits(subsetted_model)

dffits_problematic_point_indices <- which(abs(dffits) > 2*sqrt((p+1) / n))

# Influential Points: DFBETAS
dfbetas <- dfbetas(subsetted_model)
num_bad_betas <- rowSums(1*(abs(dfbetas) > 2 / sqrt(n)))

cat("Num outliers:", length(outliers_indices), "\n")
cat("Num leverage points:", length(leverage_point_indices), "\n\n")
cat("Number of problematic points determined using:\n")
cat("Cooks:", length(cooks_problematic_point_indices), "\n")
cat("DFFITS:", length(dffits_problematic_point_indices), "\n")
cat("DFBETAS:", sum(1*(num_bad_betas > 0)), "\n")
```
For visualization, I will plot the standardized residual plots
```{r standardized residuals of transformed model}
new_relevant_predictors_for_visualization <- c("PAADVVOL", "GEN_05", "GEN_01", "GEN_10")
generate_plots(subsetted_model, new_relevant_predictors_for_visualization, output_dir = "part_two/figures/standardized_residuals_transformed_model", pairwise_predictors = intersect(new_relevant_predictors_for_visualization, numeric_classes), model_data = transformed_model, standardized = TRUE)
# the plots that changed are prelim_results_resid_qq.png and prelim_results_resid_vs_pred.png
```
The plots look very similar to the plots made with non-standardized residuals.

I will be trying to reduce the number of DFFITS points. I will test the addition of every possible predictor, and read three specific outputs: 
1. How much the adjusted R2 value increases
2. How much the residuals of each problematic point drops
3. How much the residuals of each non-problematic point drops. 

We want predictors where all three hold:
- R2 value remains constant or increases
- residuals of each problematic point drops significantly
- residuals of non-problematic points don't get higher. 

```{r testing-every-new-predictor}
current_predictors <- attr(terms(subsetted_model), "term.labels")
candidate_predictors <- setdiff(non_NA, c(current_predictors, "LSM_01"))

temp_model_data <- cleaned_data |>
  drop_na(any_of(c(current_predictors, "LSM_01")))

c_val_temp <- max(temp_model_data$LBFDGHPW, na.rm = TRUE) + 1
temp_model_data$LSM_01   <- (temp_model_data$LSM_01 + 1)^2
temp_model_data$PAADVVOL <- log1p(temp_model_data$PAADVVOL)
temp_model_data$PAA_15A  <- log1p(temp_model_data$PAA_15A)
temp_model_data$LBFDGHPW <- log(c_val_temp - temp_model_data$LBFDGHPW)

# Problematic points in a model: flagged by DFFITS or an outlier (|r_i| > 4)
problematic_points <- function(m) {
  n_m <- nobs(m)
  p_m <- length(coef(m)) - 1
  abs(dffits(m)) > 2 * sqrt((p_m + 1) / n_m) | abs(rstandard(m)) > 4
}

candidate_results <- lapply(candidate_predictors, FUN = function(pred) {

  relevant_model_data <- temp_model_data |>
    drop_na(any_of(pred))

  if (nrow(relevant_model_data) < 1000) return(NULL)

  # Current model and current model + candidate, fitted on the same rows
  og_model <- lm(reformulate(current_predictors, response = "LSM_01"), data = relevant_model_data)
  model <- tryCatch(
    lm(reformulate(c(current_predictors, pred), response = "LSM_01"), data = relevant_model_data),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(model) || nobs(model) != nobs(og_model)) return(NULL)

  flagged <- problematic_points(og_model) # problematic before adding the candidate
  e_old <- abs(resid(og_model)) # how far off each prediction was
  e_new <- abs(resid(model)) # how far off it is with the candidate added

  tibble(
    predictor = pred,
    description = dict[[pred]],
    n = nobs(model),
    n_flagged = sum(flagged),
    gain_in_adj_r2 = summary(model)$adj.r.squared - summary(og_model)$adj.r.squared,
    
    # % reduction in average |residual|, for flagged points 
    pct_resid_drop_flagged = 100 * (1 - mean(e_new[flagged])  / mean(e_old[flagged])),

    # % reduction in average |residual| for all other points
    pct_resid_drop_others  = 100 * (1 - mean(e_new[!flagged]) / mean(e_old[!flagged]))
  )

}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  arrange(desc(pct_resid_drop_flagged))

candidate_results

```

From this analysis, the following predictors seemed promising (increased adjR2, decreased avg residual of problematic points by at least 1%, and also decreased avg residuals of other points):
- SLP_015 (Frequency of refreshing sleep)
- GEN_20 (sense of belonging to local community)
- COV2_005 (Self-perceived mental health before / after the pandemic)
- DHHDGHSZ (Yes = Lives alone, No = Lives with others)
- SBE_005 (Free time sitting/lying watching screen school/work day) (1200 observations remaining)
- SLP_010 (Trouble going to sleep or staying asleep)

I'll try to add the predictors of all of these except for SBE_005 since it reduces the number of observations greatly. 

```{r fitting-new-model}
new_added_predictors <- c(new_relevant_predictors, "SLP_015", "GEN_20", "COV2_005", "DHHDGHSZ", "SLP_010")

new_model_data <- cleaned_data |>
  select(any_of(c("LSM_01", new_added_predictors)))

formula <- reformulate(c(new_added_predictors, "PAADVVOL:GEN_05"), response = "LSM_01")

new_model <- lm(
  formula = formula,
  data = new_model_data
)

summary(new_model)
```

Off the bat, this added quite a few predictors that were significant. Keep in mind this does not include transformed variables, so model assumptions will need to be re-assessed. 

In particular, living alone, perceived mental health before vs after pandemic, sense of belonging to local community, and frequency of refreshing sleep came up as significant predictors.

However, the original metrics PAADVVOL (physical activity) and the interaction term with GEN_05 were still not significant. This may change after correcting model assumptions. It may also be worth looking if switching out PAADVVOL with PAA_15A would make a difference. 

Now, we will check assumptions again.

```{r visualizing-assumptions}
generate_plots(new_model, relevant_predictors = new_added_predictors[!grepl(":", new_added_predictors)], output_dir = "part_two/figures/new_model", pairwise_predictors = intersect(new_added_predictors, numeric_classes), model_data = new_model_data)
```

This shows violation of normality. Thus, Boxcox will be performed on the response in the same way as above. The right-skew for PAADVVOL will also be corrected in the same way as above. All other predictors are discrete in nature and so they will not be skew-corrected. 

```{r}
new_transformed_data <- new_model_data

# Correcting right-skew
new_transformed_data$PAADVVOL <- log1p(new_model_data$PAADVVOL)

# fitting boxcox on Y + 1 (avoids negative values)
library(car)
p <- powerTransform(new_model_data$LSM_01 + 1)

new_transformed_data$LSM_01 <- (new_model_data$LSM_01 + 1)^2

formula <- reformulate(c(new_added_predictors, "PAADVVOL:GEN_05"), response = "LSM_01")

new_boxcox_model <- lm(
  formula = formula,
  data = new_transformed_data
)

generate_plots(new_boxcox_model, relevant_predictors = new_added_predictors[!grepl(":", new_added_predictors)], output_dir = "part_two/figures/new_transformed_model", pairwise_predictors = intersect(new_added_predictors, numeric_classes), model_data = new_transformed_data)
```

This fixed normality, and variance seems to be relatively constant. Assumptions seem to hold well. 


Second round of predictor removal, keeping the interaction term PAADVVOL * GEN_05 as it is crititcal to our study.

```{r}
drop1(new_boxcox_model, test = "F")
```

```{r}
# model without SLP_010
new_boxcox_step1 <- lm(
  LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL * GEN_05 + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + SLP_015 + GEN_20 + COV2_005 + DHHDGHSZ,
  data = new_transformed_data
)

# verifying remaining predictors
drop1(new_boxcox_step1, test = "F")
```

```{r}
final_boxcox_model <- lm(
  LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL * GEN_05 + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + SLP_015 + GEN_20 + COV2_005 + DHHDGHSZ,
  data = new_transformed_data
)

# Multicollinearity check
vif(final_boxcox_model, type = "predictor")

# Residual plots
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(final_boxcox_model, main = "Final Transformed Model Diagnostics")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Coefficient table with robust standard errors
coeftest(final_boxcox_model, vcov = hccm(final_boxcox_model, type = "hc3"))
```
